note: Party set, written on 2026-11-10 by an independent writer who worked only from a brief and read no source code. The question under test is 'who is it about?'. Each case is one decide request with ONE script point and a spoken transcript of one or two sentences in which the point's own words (or close ones) appear, so that only the party decides. A point is either about the speaker's own side (their company, school, team, club, shop) or about someone else (a competitor, a supplier, a customer, a regulator, a partner, a named person, the market). Convention: a point counts as covered only when the transcript says it of the same party the point means. P001 to P040 should be ticked: own-plain (P001-P010, the point is about the speaker's side and the speaker says it of their side), third-party-point (P011-P020, the point itself names someone else and the transcript says it of that same someone), own-implicit (P021-P030, a bare label with no owner, spoken of with no owner word or in the passive), market-or-general (P031-P040, the point is about a market, a law, a trend or people in general). P041 to P080 must NOT be ticked: supplier-or-partner (P041-P050), competitor (P051-P060), customer-or-other-person (P061-P070), where the point is about the speaker's side and the transcript says it of that other party, and wrong-third-party (P071-P080), where the point names one third party and the transcript says it of a different one. Languages: 30 en, 30 it, 4 each of ro, ru, ja, es, de; point and transcript are in the same language. covered is true, false, or null when two careful listeners could disagree (null is not counted). Labels are one writer's judgement after a second strict pass.
